texts.orig: The goal of this project is to design an alarm clock uƟlizing the tools and equipment that we have learned about up to this point in the semester. Technical requirements for the design of the alarm were to include a potenƟometer to adjust Ɵme, incorporate at least one switch to control the countdown, use a seven-segment display to visibly display the countdown, and to sound an audible alarm with a piezo buzzer. This set up is a very simple, but applicable design to show how a countdown Ɵmer might perform on a small scale. To accomplish this goal, I knew I wanted to add addiƟonal switches to beƩer control the funcƟons of starƟng, stopping, and adjusƟng the alarm clock countdown. The potenƟometer, piezo buzzer, and seven segment display were easy to visualize and incorporate due to recent experience in other lab assignments. In terms of design layout, I wanted to keep it simple and easy for me to keep track of. I first built a circuit that included all required equipment and assigned pins to necessary inputs and outputs. Reusing some coding and circuit layout from previous exercises, including Lab 4, Lab 3, and Lab 2 material streamlined this process.

texts.orig: Building the circuit for the alarm clock was streamlined by reusing concepts from previous lab assignments. Seƫng up the 4 digit 7-segment display followed the procedure listed in lab 4. Then I connected the three switches to analog pins, with each switch grounded with resistors. Next, I placed the potenƟometer connected to power and ground with the middle pin connected to A0 pin. Finally, I added the piezo to connect to pin A4 and ground.
